newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine budget not ready for planned Jun 2 reading.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine budget not ready for planned Jun 2 reading.

text.p: Ukraine's government had still not returned this year's budget draft to parliament on Monday, a spokesman said -- meaning a planned second reading of the much-delayed document could not go ahead on Tuesday.
Approval of the budget would ease the way to a $2.5-$3 billion, three-year Extended Fund Facility loan from the International Monetary Fund.
"This issue was not considered today," a cabinet spokesman told Reuters when asked if the draft had been passed on.

Parliament, which sent the budget back to the government to be reworked after its first reading in December, had been scheduled to reconsider it from Tuesday, First Deputy Finance Minister Stanislav Bukovinsky said last Friday.

UNIAN news agency quoted Viktor Suslov, head of parliament's finance and banking committee, as saying the cabinet planned to approve the revamped document on Wednesday so it would be ready for a second reading in parliament on Thursday and Friday.
President Leonid Kuchma has proposed a compromise to the conservative-dominated parliament where the budget would be approved on the basis of two out of a package of nine tough tax reforms.
His press service said at the weekend that the budget would be approved on the basis of a value added tax and enterprise profit tax which have already been approved.
Gross Domestic Product has been forecast at 100.4 billion hryvnias ($54.6 billion) and the deficit stood at 5.7 percent compared to 6.2 percent last year.
Annual inflation is forecast in the draft at 24.9 percent after 39.7 percent in 1996.
